From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Admin onramp + API seeding plan for SkyBridge — initial coordination

Hi Emily — great to meet you on the call yesterday. Per our onboarding checklist I’m sending a short plan for how we handle SkyBridge’s initial org entry and API key seeding so you have visibility and we can move to invites quickly.

High level proposal (2-step onramp):
1) Admin doorway (day 0–1): seed 2 admin users (org admin + security admin), create primary project namespace, enable SSO flag if you want us to prepare SAML metadata, and invite your initial admin roster.
2) Developer sandbox & API key seeding (day 1–3): provision 1 sandbox project for engineering, generate scoped API keys (read-only / dev / prod-sim), and hand over a short key-rotation guidance doc.

What we need from you to start:
- Confirm two admin contacts (name + email) to seed as Org Admin and Security Admin.
- Preferred project naming convention (we’ve included a template).
- Whether you want SSO setup before invites (we can invite admins with provisional passwords until SSO is ready).
- Any IP allowlist or more restrictive policies for initial keys.

Attached: redwood-admin-onramp-checklist.csv, api-key-seeding-policy.md, project-namespace-template.xlsx.

Proposed timelines: we can do admin invites today and seed sandbox keys tomorrow afternoon. If you prefer a single day handoff we can compress to the morning.

Next step: reply with admin contacts and any must-have constraints and I’ll route to Dev to seed keys and to Monica to schedule the invite wave.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: redwood-admin-onramp-checklist.csv (CSV, 12 rows), api-key-seeding-policy.md (Markdown, 3 pages)

Thanks — quick technical note on the seeding steps and what I’ll perform: 

1) Create org "skybridge-systems" and seed users Martin Cho and Priya Nair with Admin and Security Admin roles. I’ll tag the accounts with external_admin=true to make them explicit in auditing.
2) Create project namespaces per naming convention; I’ll create sbg-dev-platform and sbg-prod-core as placeholders. We will not generate prod-scoped keys until you request them in writing (Emily).
3) Generate sandbox keys with scopes: write:dev, read:all (dev-only). Attach IP restrictions to the key metadata (13.54.32.0/22 + CI ranges). Keys will be created as "ephemeral" with a 90-day rotation flag by default.
4) If SSO metadata is provided, I’ll upload SAML settings to the org and mark the admin accounts as federated after the handshake completes (preferred).

I’ll document the key fingerprints and create a short handoff doc in Drive (link to follow). If Monica wants provisional invites while SSO is pending, I can also create temporary passwords that expire after 24 hours.
